instructor:
He's not interested in teaching us anything useful. This can be seen in the assignments given. If the course was given in 2000s, maybe assignment's style would make sense, but in the age of tensorflow/pytorch, coding various neural networks yourself does not make sense. One of the strongest suits of those APIs (Tensorflow etc.) is their ability to do automatic differentiation, meaning that you only need to code the forward pass of the network, the backward-pass will be done for you in an efficient way. This enables extremely quick experimentation (finding the backward-pass and implementing it is a fool's job nowadays and extremely time-consuming). However, these are not pointed out in the lectures or in the assignments. Mini-project was the worst of all. We were asked to implement many types of neural networks (without TF, of course). It did not promote any learning of the materials. Since we coded them ourselves, their performance was extremely poor and training anything would take a lot of time, therefore was not helpful to us, the students.
To students who are planning to take this course: if you are planning to learn anything, DO NOT take this course, it might result in you hating this exciting field of artificial intelligence. However, if you just want to get a high grade and do not care about how bad you will spend your time, go ahead. This course does not have any examinations, but beware, you might start to lose your interest in this field.
If Bilkent wants to step up their game, they need to fundamentally change courses like this (that wastes time while claiming to teach an important subject). Otherwise, its ranking, only supported by the most hardworking and intelligent students in the country, is doomed to continue to fall into the abyss.
